checks.evidence: Proofs are in core: lint lifecycle cases EditedBesideAnExcludedFile and PartialOfAReusedFileAfterAFileIsListedBeforeIt, and recording service_test, on fixture repositories and a fake store.

stored_of (domain/handing/service.rs:241) stores a part of the record's own file as OneFile(PartialAt(0)). partials_of (:155) maps any OneFile back to the reusing run's number `own`, and hand_rest_again passes `number`, the file's number in this run. interface_bytes (recording/service.rs) now digests stored_of(.., number), so the interface digest no longer changes when the file is renumbered, which mirrors moved_words. The new case lints [a, b], then [a, a2, b] over the same store with b reused at a new number, and compares the edit run's rows, unknowns and kept covered rows with a cold run of the three files. On the old code the edit store keeps b's part at the old number 1 while the cold store keeps it at 2, so the covered comparison fails. In the run itself b's part would name a2, which drops b's Unknown, so the rows/unknowns comparison fails too. The guard assertion requires the cold store to hold a part for b, so the case cannot pass vacuously. The read_alone fix is unchanged from the first review (correct). The test is unrun (hook); the integrator runs it.
One position-independent form for a file's own facts (words and parts at 0), one numbering for the run.

judgement_other_file_part: The builder's claim holds today, so the Repository widening loses nothing now. A file's `said` parts (parsing/service.rs:147-240 into start_partials → coverage::partial_of) come from three sources: the engine rows (OneFile of the file's own number, parsing/service.rs:354, reading/service.rs:124); a provider's per-file `partial` statement, which the facts writer records as Repository (execution_runtime/src/outbound/facts/types.rs:99-105); and recoveries, which are Repository (coverage/service.rs:239-244). `partial_at <file>`, the only way to name another file, appears only in project-scope items (manifests/ and links/ collections of go, javascript, python, rust and typescript). Those parts go to the project phase (application/file_analysis/project/service.rs:101-104), which is recomputed every run and never kept per file. So no per-file record can hold a part of another file now. If one ever did, widening it to Repository makes more rules Unknown. That is a coverage change, but it is visible: it changes the report's unknowns, which byte checks compare. It is still wider than the truth, so a mechanical guard is offered (candidate per-file-partial-names-another-file-2a55efb0).
